input: Landed at Changi at last. My suitcase came off the belt with a wheel missing and I am too wrung out to queue at the desk about it.
Back in my own flat. The basil on the windowsill has collapsed completely but the spider plant looks smug.
The last of the guests from Dad's seventieth have just gone. I have washed something like forty glasses and I am sitting in the kitchen next to an empty cake stand.
Gone twelve now. My brother Callum stayed behind with the end of the port and we have dragged two chairs out onto the patio.
He has just told me he is taking the job in Aberdeen in the new year. I was not ready for how much that would sting.
He has gone up to bed. I am stacking the folding chairs in the hall, slowly, one at a time.
Found one last sausage roll under a sheet of foil and ate it cold, standing over the bin.
Still up. I keep wondering who is going to do Sunday lunch with Dad once Callum has moved.
Oh, the clocks have just gone back. The cooker says quarter past one all over again, so I have been handed this hour twice.
Right, that is me. Lights off.
What did I tell you on Saturday night before midnight, and what came once it was past midnight?
Which did I mention first, the last sausage roll or the clocks going back?
And what day did my flight get in on that trip?
